text: Tell me about yourself.
tip: A good answer is a short story: your current role, key experience, and why you want this job. About one minute.

text: Why do you want to work for our company?
tip: Mention specific things about the company and connect them to your skills.

text: What is your greatest strength?
tip: Pick one strength that matters for the job and support it with a short example.

text: What is your biggest weakness?
tip: Choose a real but minor weakness and explain what you are doing to improve it.

text: Tell me about a time you worked in a team to solve a problem.
tip: Use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result.

text: Describe a time you disagreed with a colleague. How did you handle it?
tip: Show calm, respectful communication and a positive outcome.

text: Tell me about a mistake you made at work and what you learned from it.
tip: Take responsibility, do not blame others, and focus on the lesson.

text: How do you handle stress and tight deadlines?
tip: Give a concrete method, such as prioritizing or planning, and a short example.

text: Tell me about a time you led a project or a group of people.
tip: Describe how you motivated people and what result you achieved.

text: Where do you see yourself in five years?
tip: Show ambition that fits the company. Avoid being vague or unrealistic.

text: What are your salary expectations?
tip: Give a researched range and show that you are flexible.

text: Why are you leaving your current job?
tip: Stay positive. Talk about growth and new challenges, not complaints.

text: Describe a difficult problem you solved. What steps did you take?
tip: Explain your thinking clearly, step by step.

text: Tell me about something new you learned recently and how you learned it.
tip: This shows curiosity and the ability to learn independently.

text: Tell me about a time you helped a customer or colleague who was upset.
tip: Show empathy, careful listening and a practical solution.

text: Do you have any questions for us?
tip: Always ask one or two thoughtful questions about the role or the team.

text: What would you do if you were given a task you had never done before?
tip: Show initiative: research, ask questions and ask for feedback early.

text: How do you decide what to do first when you have many tasks?
tip: Mention priorities, deadlines and communication with your manager.

text: What is your favourite food, and can you cook it yourself?
tip: Encourage full sentences and food vocabulary such as ingredients and flavours.

text: What do you like to do in your free time?
tip: Ask follow-up questions about how often and why.

text: Tell me about a place you would love to visit and why.
tip: Practise conditionals: I would like to..., If I went there, I would...

text: What did you do last weekend?
tip: Good for practising the past simple tense.

text: What are your plans for next weekend?
tip: Practise future forms: going to, will, present continuous.

text: Tell me about your family or a friend you are close to.
tip: Practise describing people with adjectives.

text: What is the weather like where you live, and which season do you like best?
tip: Practise comparatives and weather vocabulary.

text: How do you use technology in your daily life?
tip: Introduce vocabulary about phones, apps and the internet.

text: What kind of movies or music do you enjoy?
tip: Ask for opinions and reasons: I like it because...

text: Describe a typical day in your life from morning to night.
tip: Practise the present simple and time expressions.

text: What was your favourite thing to do as a child?
tip: Practise used to and the past simple.

text: If you could learn any new skill instantly, what would it be?
tip: Practise the second conditional: If I could..., I would...

text: Ask the learner to write three sentences about things they did yesterday, then three about things they have done in their life.
tip: Check the difference between finished time (yesterday) and experience (ever, already).

text: Give the learner five sentences with a gap and ask them to fill in the past form of an irregular verb such as go, eat, see, buy or take.
tip: Common errors: goed, eated, buyed.

text: Ask the learner to describe their room using a, an and the correctly.
tip: Check a and an for first mention, and the for things already known.

text: Ask the learner to write sentences about what their family members do every day.
tip: Common errors: she don't, he go. He, she and it need an -s in the present simple.

text: Ask the learner to complete sentences with in, on or at for times and dates.
tip: in the morning, on Monday, at five o'clock.

text: Ask the learner to finish the sentence: If I had more free time, I would... with three different endings.
tip: Check had in the if-part and would in the result.

text: Ask the learner to give advice to a friend who is always tired, using should, must and could.
tip: After a modal verb, the next verb has no -s and no to.

text: Ask the learner to compare three cities or three foods using comparatives and superlatives.
tip: Check -er and -est, more and most, and irregular forms such as better and best.

text: Ask the learner to turn five statements into questions using do, does, did and question words.
tip: Check the helping verb and the word order.

text: Ask the learner to write sentences about food using much, many, a few and a little.
tip: Common errors: many water, much apples.

text: Ask the learner to talk about plans with going to and about predictions with will.
tip: Use going to for plans, and will for sudden decisions and predictions.

text: Give two short sentences that someone said and ask the learner to report them using said that.
tip: Check the tense shift: I am tired becomes She said she was tired.
